sections.text: Result is an enum for operations that can fail. Ok holds the success value, Err holds the error. In Result<T, E>, T is the type of the success value and E is the type of the error, so Result<f64, String> means "an f64 on success, or a String describing the error".

parse turns text into a number, and gives back a Result because the text might not be a number. The type Result<i32, _> tells parse to make an i32; the _ lets Rust fill in the error type itself. You'll also see the type written on the call instead: "12".parse::<i32>(). The ::<i32> part means the same thing, "parse as an i32".
Handle both cases with match. The compiler won't let you use the value without dealing with the error first:
Like Option, Result has helpers such as unwrap_or and is_ok:
Errors are ordinary values, not hidden jumps. Reading a function's signature tells you whether it can fail.
No exceptions: Result<T, E> is Rust's error-handling mechanism, and #[must_use] warns if you ignore one. map_err, ok() and and_then convert and chain results.
